design: Probe CPU model/cores/ISA, RAM, GPU/Metal/CUDA/Vulkan devices, unified memory; map to available llama.cpp backends
acceptance_criteria: `ucompute hardware --json` reports chip, physical cores, total memory and every usable backend; values match sysctl/system_profiler (macOS) or /proc + lspci (Linux) on each tested host; completes in <2 s; runs unprivileged
observed_evidence: docs/VERIFICATION.md F-01-01: probe matches sysctl, 41-56 ms, unprivileged (macOS only; Linux/Windows fixture-tested, B-004)

description: GGUF model loading and streaming inference.
design: Load GGUF via llama.cpp, expose token stream; read GGUF metadata (arch, layers, ctx, quant, tokenizer)
acceptance_criteria: With a pinned real GGUF and seed, greedy generation reproduces a stored golden token sequence on the same backend; first token is delivered before generation finishes; truncated/corrupt GGUF files return a typed error and never crash (fuzz 1,000 mutated headers)
observed_evidence: docs/VERIFICATION.md F-01-02: golden text CPU+Metal, replay reproduces token ids, streaming before done, 2x1000 fuzz no panic

design: Estimate weights + KV cache + compute buffers from GGUF metadata and context length; compare to free memory
acceptance_criteria: For >=5 models/quant/context combinations, predicted peak memory is within +/-15% of measured peak RSS (or Metal allocation); models predicted not to fit are refused before load with a plain-language reason
observed_evidence: docs/VERIFICATION.md F-01-03/F-01-08: 14 combos within -4.6..+8.9% of measured engine footprint; refusal with plain-language reason

analogy: FFmpeg hardware decode with software fallback
design: Select GPU backend (Metal/CUDA/Vulkan) when available, offload N layers, fall back to CPU on init failure
acceptance_criteria: On a Metal host: GPU path is selected by default, reports offloaded layer count, and decode tok/s is recorded vs CPU for the same model; greedy output matches CPU within a documented tolerance (identical tokens for first 32 tokens on the pinned fixture); simulated GPU init failure falls back to CPU with a logged reason, never silently
observed_evidence: docs/VERIFICATION.md F-01-04: Metal default with log-proven offload, forced-GPU-failure fallback with reason, CPU vs Metal benchmarks in benchmarks/results/

description: Model download, integrity checks, and cache.
design: HTTP(S) download into content-addressed cache with SHA-256 verification against manifest
acceptance_criteria: Downloading a pinned model produces a cache entry whose SHA-256 equals the manifest; a single flipped byte causes rejection and deletion of the partial file; second request is served from cache with zero network bytes; pinned engine archives are SHA-256 verified before extraction, extraction refuses traversal/absolute/escaping-symlink members, and every extracted file is re-verified against the archive
observed_evidence: docs/VERIFICATION.md F-01-05: cache hit 0 bytes, flipped byte rejected + partial deleted, https-only, safe extraction + re-verify; real HF pull verified

design: Rust trait InferenceBackend {load, generate, cancel, capabilities}; llama.cpp is first impl; registry by name
acceptance_criteria: Backend conformance test suite passes for llama.cpp adapter and for at least one additional real backend (e.g., MLX or a separately built llama.cpp variant); swapping backend requires no change outside the adapter crate
observed_evidence: docs/VERIFICATION.md: InferenceBackend trait + conformance suite pass for llama.cpp (7 checks)
blocker: Acceptance needs a second real backend passing the conformance suite (none implemented yet)

design: Given free memory and target context, rank available quantizations of the same model by fit then quality
acceptance_criteria: For a model offered in >=3 quantizations, the recommendation is the highest-bit quantization whose F-01-03 estimate fits with >=10% headroom; recommendation is never applied without user confirmation (no silent substitution)
observed_evidence: crates/ucompute-models quant.rs recommend() + tests (highest-bit fit with headroom, confirmation required); QuantType FromStr
blocker: No CLI/API surface yet (ucompute models recommend / API field); recommendation not reachable by users

design: Plan n_ctx and KV cache type (f16/q8) within memory budget; cap at model trained context
acceptance_criteria: Requested context above the model's trained context is refused or capped with an explicit message; KV cache bytes predicted within +/-10% of measured; prompt longer than n_ctx returns a typed error, not truncated silently
observed_evidence: docs/VERIFICATION.md F-01-03/F-01-08: KV bytes exact vs engine log; cap/refuse above trained ctx with context_note; prompt > n_ctx typed error

design: Image input via llama.cpp multimodal (mtmd) projector GGUFs
acceptance_criteria: A pinned vision GGUF + projector answers a fixed image prompt with a golden token sequence under fixed seed; image size limits enforced

design: Draft-model speculative decoding via llama.cpp; record acceptance rate
acceptance_criteria: Greedy output with speculative decoding is token-identical to the target model alone; speedup and acceptance rate are measured and reported; feature is disabled automatically when measured speedup < 1.0

design: Load/unload LoRA GGUF adapters with scale; hash-pinned in manifest
acceptance_criteria: Applying a pinned LoRA produces logits that differ from base and match a golden; incompatible base/adapter pair is refused with reason; adapter hash verified

design: JSON-schema to GBNF grammar constrained decoding; OpenAI tools/function-call request and response shapes
acceptance_criteria: 100/100 constrained generations validate against the supplied JSON schema; an unmodified official OpenAI client parses tool-call responses; pathological grammars are rejected within a time/size bound

acceptance_criteria: Packet capture of a remote inference session contains no plaintext prompt or token strings; connection with an unpinned key is refused; transport overhead on decode TPOT measured (H1 target <=5%)

design: Versioned capability record: hardware, backends, free memory, cached model hashes, protocol versions
acceptance_criteria: After handshake each peer holds the other's capability record matching its local `ucompute hardware --json`; messages over the size bound are rejected and logged
observed_evidence: capabilities_exchanged_after_handshake (received hardware_json equals the sender's probe, the source of ucompute hardware --json); capabilities signed over the exact bytes sent (SignedCapabilities); oversized_capability_message_rejected (FrameTooLarge, closed, audited peer_rejected reason frame_too_large). design: Heartbeat with configurable interval; mark peer unhealthy after N misses; QUIC idle timeout
acceptance_criteria: Killing a peer process (SIGKILL) is detected within 3 heartbeat intervals (default <=6 s); network partition detected within the same bound; recovery restores healthy state
observed_evidence: kill_peer_detected_within_bound_single_host and sigkill_peer_process_detected_within_bound_single_host (separate OS process); daemon run SIGKILL detected in 4.855 s and 4.879 s (bound 6 s); partition_detected_and_recovered_single_host (Reconnecting within 6 s, recovered to Connected); restart reconnects in 3.7-3.8 s. design: Hole punching with relay fallback (evaluate iroh 1.0 vs libp2p DCUtR); relays see only ciphertext
acceptance_criteria: In a netns NAT matrix (full-cone, restricted, symmetric) connections succeed directly where possible and via relay otherwise; relay traffic is end-to-end encrypted; success rate reported per NAT type

design: Active RTT pings and bounded bandwidth probe; passive measurement from real traffic
acceptance_criteria: Under netem-imposed 20 ms RTT and 100 Mbit/s, measured RTT within +/-20% and bandwidth within +/-25%; probes never exceed a configured byte budget

design: Choose paths/relays and stage order to minimize measured RTT across topology
acceptance_criteria: With three peers under asymmetric netem latencies, the chosen pipeline order minimizes summed hop RTT (verified against brute force)

design: Named groups of pinned keys with per-group policy; persisted in SQLite
acceptance_criteria: Workloads tagged for a group are never dispatched to non-members (asserted in integration test); group state survives restart
observed_evidence: group_membership_crud; peer_store_persists_across_reopen (groups, pins and revocations survive restart); workload_only_to_group_members, non_member_rejected (policy); unauthorized_peer_is_refused (integration: pinned non-member gets peer_unauthorized, nothing executed); local_only_never_leaves_device_10k_single_host covers group policy combinations. design: Adjust batch size, chunking and placement to measured link quality; never change model/quant/privacy silently
acceptance_criteria: When link bandwidth drops 10x mid-session, the system adapts transport parameters or proposes fallback; model hash, quantization and privacy mode in the execution record are unchanged unless the user consents

design: Kademlia-style DHT or iroh discovery for peers beyond LAN; signed records with expiry
acceptance_criteria: Peers on separate simulated networks discover each other without a central server; unsigned/expired records are ignored; eclipse simulation documented with results

design: Prefer peers by measured RTT, optional coarse self-declared region; no IP geolocation by default
acceptance_criteria: Peer selection orders candidates by measured RTT; self-declared regions are advisory and never used to satisfy a privacy/jurisdiction constraint without verification

design: Split transformer layers [0,k) and [k,n) between two processes/hosts; each loads only its layers' weights
acceptance_criteria: Two independent physical machines each load only their layer range (verified by per-process memory), exchange activations over the encrypted transport, and produce tokens; single-host multiprocess runs are recorded separately and labelled SINGLE-HOST
observed_evidence: docs/evidence/pool-two-machine-2026-11-06.md: this Mac and sentinel, 23 steps 0 FAIL at 1038a7f, placement proved at -lv 4, activations over the encrypted transport, tokens produced (TWO-MACHINE)
blocker: Per-process memory on both hosts not recorded yet (plan P1.5); the acceptance criterion requires it

design: Per-stage weight and KV memory accounting reported in execution record
acceptance_criteria: Each node's measured peak memory is below the full-model single-node peak by at least the size of the layers it does not host (+/-15%), recorded in the execution record
blocker: Real verification requires two independent physical machines

design: Length-prefixed, versioned activation frames (hidden_dim x dtype x tokens); bounded size; ordered per request
acceptance_criteria: Bytes per decoded token per boundary measured and equal to hidden_dim x element_size (+ framing <=64 B); frames with wrong dimension or over size bound are rejected without crash

design: Compare partitioned vs local logits on identical backend/model/seed
acceptance_criteria: On the same backend and F32 fixture, split execution logits equal local logits within max-abs 1e-4 for every generated position (1e-3 for quantized), and greedy tokens are identical for >=64 tokens; test asserts real inference occurred (non-empty, non-error)

design: Choose split points minimizing predicted TPOT subject to per-node memory
acceptance_criteria: Chosen split is within 10% of the best measured split across a grid of split points on the 2-3 node test cluster

design: Overlap stages across micro-batches/concurrent requests
acceptance_criteria: With 4 concurrent requests, aggregate throughput exceeds single-request throughput on the same split; outputs per request identical to sequential execution

design: Allocate layers proportional to measured per-device throughput and memory
acceptance_criteria: On two devices with >=2x throughput difference, balanced allocation beats an equal split in measured TPOT, or the scheduler selects local-only if that is faster

design: Route whole requests to replicas by queue depth and health
acceptance_criteria: Under 50 concurrent requests across 3 workers, max/min per-worker request count ratio <=1.5; unhealthy worker receives zero new requests

design: Per-stage KV ownership; KV transfer for prefill/decode disaggregation (H3)
acceptance_criteria: Decode after KV transfer produces tokens identical to uninterrupted local decode; transfer time and bytes recorded

design: On stage failure: abort request with typed error, or re-place stage and replay prompt
acceptance_criteria: Killing a stage mid-generation yields either a typed error within 10 s or a completed response after re-placement; no hung request; recovery time recorded

design: Split weight matrices within layers with all-reduce; only enabled where measured link latency permits
acceptance_criteria: Tensor-parallel logits match local within tolerance; measured TPOT vs local reported; scheduler refuses TP when measured all-reduce latency makes it slower (research: latency-bound, see RESEARCH_GAPS 2.1)

design: Move layer ranges between peers between requests (and mid-session with KV migration later)
acceptance_criteria: After a peer joins/leaves, the next request uses a new partition; outputs remain correct vs local; repartition time recorded

design: Filter candidate plans by memory, backend support, policy and trust before scoring
acceptance_criteria: Property test over 10,000 random cluster states: no emitted plan exceeds any node's free memory or violates the request's privacy policy

design: Deterministic rules: local if fits, else smallest feasible trusted split; stable tie-breaking
acceptance_criteria: Identical inputs produce byte-identical plans across 100 runs and across processes

design: Compare predicted local vs distributed TTFT/TPOT; refuse distribution when predicted to regress (H2)
acceptance_criteria: Across the measured grid (models x links x device pairs) decision accuracy >=90% and no chosen plan regresses >10% vs local

design: Cost model: compute time per layer (measured), transfer = bytes/bandwidth + RTT per hop, separate prefill/decode, cold/warm load
acceptance_criteria: Predicted TTFT and TPOT within +/-25% of measured for >=80% of grid points

design: Rank peers by measured RTT and stability
acceptance_criteria: With netem latencies 1/10/50 ms, scheduler selects the 1 ms peer first in every trial

design: Separate placement for compute-bound prefill vs bandwidth-bound decode
acceptance_criteria: For >=2K-token prompts on a heterogeneous pair, PD-aware plan's end-to-end latency is measured vs static split; feature disabled automatically where it regresses (H3)

design: Feedback loop updates cost model from execution records; tune batch/threads
acceptance_criteria: After 20 requests, measured throughput is >= baseline config; any change that regresses >5% is reverted automatically

design: Prefer nodes with model chunks already cached/loaded
acceptance_criteria: Given equal compute, node with warm model is selected; TTFT warm vs cold measured and recorded

design: Energy objective using measured power (powermetrics/RAPL where available) or documented estimates
acceptance_criteria: Where power telemetry exists, joules/token measured; energy-preferring policy selects the lower-J/token plan; where telemetry is absent, UI states 'estimated'

design: Penalize peers with high churn/failure history
acceptance_criteria: Peer with injected 30% failure rate receives <10% of placements after 20 requests when alternatives exist

design: Forecast whether queued workload fits cluster capacity
acceptance_criteria: Capacity forecast for a fixed workload trace predicts queueing delay within +/-30% of measured

design: Weighted speed/cost/privacy/energy objectives; privacy is a hard constraint, others weighted
acceptance_criteria: Changing objective weights changes chosen plan as predicted in unit tests; no weighting can produce a privacy-violating plan (property test)

design: Manifest: model name, version, file SHA-256, size, license, source URL, chunk list
acceptance_criteria: Every cached model has a manifest whose hash matches file content; loading a file whose hash mismatches the manifest fails
observed_evidence: docs/VERIFICATION.md F-01-05/F-05-01: manifests + sha256 store; tampered blob rejected before engine spawn

design: HTTP Range resume with partial-file hash continuation
acceptance_criteria: Download killed at 50% resumes without re-downloading completed bytes (network bytes <= remaining +1 chunk) and final hash verifies
observed_evidence: docs/VERIFICATION.md F-05-02: cut_at_half_then_resume test; real HF download killed at 156.1 MB resumed from that offset and verified

design: LRU with size cap and pinning; never evict a model in use
acceptance_criteria: Cache never exceeds configured cap after any operation; pinned and in-use models are never evicted

design: Record license from manifest/GGUF metadata; surface before download/run
acceptance_criteria: License shown before first run for every catalog model; unknown license is labelled 'unknown', not omitted
observed_evidence: docs/VERIFICATION.md F-05-04: license shown in models list, before pull, and in the desktop download dialog; unknown labelled unknown

design: Fixed-size chunks addressed by BLAKE3/SHA-256
acceptance_criteria: Chunking then reassembling any model reproduces identical bytes; each chunk is addressable by hash

design: Fetch chunks from paired peers before internet; respect redistribution policy
acceptance_criteria: Second and third devices obtain a 1+ GB model from LAN peers with zero integrity failures; time-to-ready measured vs WAN download (H4); models without redistribution permission are never served

design: Store identical chunks once across models/versions
acceptance_criteria: Two model files sharing chunks consume disk equal to unique chunks (+metadata); deleting one keeps the other intact

design: Fetch only tensors/chunks needed for an assigned layer range
acceptance_criteria: A pipeline stage hosting layers [k,n) downloads <=(its share + shared tensors + 1 chunk) of model bytes

design: Verify each chunk hash on receipt; ban peers serving bad chunks
acceptance_criteria: Injected corrupt chunk is rejected, re-fetched from another source, and the serving peer's reputation is penalized

design: Execution manifests pin exact model hash; no implicit upgrades
acceptance_criteria: A request pinned to hash H runs H or fails; it never runs a different version

design: Track chunk replication across peers; proactively replicate under-replicated chunks within quotas
acceptance_criteria: Chunks below target replication reach it within a bounded time in a 4-node test without exceeding any node's storage quota

design: Prefetch likely-needed models/chunks during idle time within quotas
acceptance_criteria: Prefetch occurs only when allowed (idle, unmetered, within quota) and measurably reduces TTFT on the predicted next request

analogy: SSH host keys / Tailscale node keys
